analysis.title: Buckling up
key_insights: Markets face a heavy week: FOMC meeting, PCE data, month-end Treasury auctions and month-end index extension on Friday.
House view is for the FOMC to hold rates this week and hike in December. Markets price little chance of a hike this week and about 22bp of tightening by year-end.

AI jitters and volatility in European government bonds created haven demand for Treasuries, taking the 10Y yield back to 5.00%, 30bp below the early-October peak and right on its 50-day moving average.
A rally in energy markets pushed yields modestly higher last Friday.

September core PCE is forecast near the rounding cusp between 0.3% and 0.4% MoM, with YoY rising to 3.1% from 3.0%. This is not ideal for the Fed, though core FOMC members have suggested a bias towards holding in October.
Coupon supply is heavy: USD69bn 2Y on Monday, USD70bn 5Y on Tuesday and USD44bn 7Y on Thursday.
The desk favours curve flatteners: with little near-term Fed action the front end is anchored, and flight-to-quality trades would benefit the long end.
Relative value: long 10Y versus 5Y and 30Y, as the 10Y looks cheap.

Base case is that Democrats regain the House in the mid-term elections, producing legislative gridlock whichever party holds the Senate. A divided government would cut the odds of major spending programmes and tax cuts, easing term premium and long-end yields and supporting a flatter curve.
